title: Finite affine cover bound from affine-local restriction acyclicity
statement: Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec} A$ be separated, with $A$ commutative, and let $i:Z\to X$ be any morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $J$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Assume that for every affine open $W\subseteq X$ and every $k>0$, $H^k(W\times_X Z,(J|_W)|_{W\times_X Z})=0$, using inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and underlying abelian cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. If $X$ has an affine open cover indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)$, then $H^q(Z,i^{-1}J)=0$ for every $q>n$. No injectivity, torsion, or closed-immersion assumption is made.

source.place: Proof, Mayer-Vietoris induction (step 6 of the parent node)

proof.text: For n=0 the single affine member is all of X. Apply the local hypothesis through the identity pullback and inverse-image comparisons.

For n+1 split the cover into an affine U and the union V of n+1 other affine opens. Since X is separated over an affine scheme, each intersection U with an affine member is affine, giving n+1 affine opens covering U intersect V.
The affine-local hypothesis descends to the restrictions on V and U intersect V by composition of inverse images and associativity of pullbacks. Induction gives bounds n on both; U has bound zero.

Pull back U,V to a cover of Z. The Mayer-Vietoris exact segment has degree q-1 on the intersection on its left and degree q on each open on its right. For q>n+1 these outer groups vanish, so its middle group is zero. Transport the derived-global-sections computation to the canonical abelian cohomology groups.
